body:
## The REASON line this anchor asks for: **AssertionError, ⛔ not a timeout**

Read from both victim builds' job logs, one of which (#17982) is this seat's PR. The anchor's own instruction is that "a timeout and an assertion are the same FAIL line and opposite diagnoses" — so here is the discrimination, identical at both victims:

```
FAIL  integration  test/format-zod-union.test.ts
  > [#5341] `os validate` delivers a union branch prescription
  > the specimen fails on exactly one issue, and that issue is the union      line 205:20
  > leaves the `--json` payload exactly as it was — full, and nested          line 227:28
AssertionError: expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
  - Expected 1
  + Received 2
```

| | #17982 build `34758691525` | #18014 build `34756944488` |
|---|---|---|
| failing job | `Test Core (3/6)` → *Run this shard's tests* | `Test Core (3/6)` → *Run this shard's tests* |
| failing assertions | lines **205** and **227** | lines **205** and **227** |
| reason | `AssertionError`, length 1 → **2** | `AssertionError`, length 1 → **2** |
| shard command | `@objectstack/cli … --shard=1/2` | `@objectstack/cli … --shard=1/2` |
| rest of the shard | 126 files / 1824 tests **passed** | 1826 test(s) declared, all accounted for |

⇒ **The load/timing-cliff branch of this anchor's four-way is ruled out.** Nothing timed out; the suite ran to completion and two assertions disagreed about a count. A slow runner does not turn one zod issue into two.

## Control — `main` itself is GREEN on this test

`CI` on `main` (push event), same period:

| head | created | conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| `1e20f816e` | 2026-09-13T12:51:16Z | **success** |
| `f52bfa90f` | 2026-09-13T12:42:00Z | **success** |

⇒ it is **not** a plain regression that any branch build would show. The divergence is between the merge-queue tree and the branch/push tree, which is itself the finding.

## What that leaves, stated as a hypothesis and ⛔ not as a result

Of the anchor's four candidates, **flake** and **load/timing cliff** are ruled out above; **plain regression** is ruled out by the `main` control. The remaining one is a **semantic conflict between queued PRs** — two changes that are each green alone and disagree once stacked.

⚠️ ⛔ **I have NOT measured which pair.** That is the open question, and it is the whole question.

## The cheapest next probe, so the taker does not restart from zero

The assertion throws away the evidence it needs: `toHaveLength(1)` reports the count and never the contents. Build the queue tree (or any tree where it reproduces) and print **both** issues — `code` and `path` for each — instead of asserting the length. The **second** issue's `path` names the schema that started emitting it, which names the change that introduced it. One run, and the conflict stops being a guess.

## Lane reading — an input to triage, ⛔ not a label

The failing file is `packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts`. Per `references/lanes/cli.md`, `packages/cli` is **`domain:cli`**. ⛔ This (`domain:services`) seat holds zero of it and has labelled nothing here.

## What the victim PR did

#17982 changes **2** files, both `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/*.test.ts`; `packages/cli` hits: **0**. Its own branch CI at `b4246a6bf` was 34 check runs, 30 success + 4 skipped, **0 failing**. It is standing down on this failure rather than fixing it (another lane), spending its one sanctioned re-queue, and ⛔ has not skipped, quarantined or weakened this test — which is also what this anchor's own text says no one should do.

## Second reproduction — and it was on a **different merge base**, which kills the stack-conflict hypothesis

PR #17982 ejected again, build [`34759517090`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34759517090), same job `Test Core (3/6)`, same two assertions (lines 205 / 227), same `AssertionError: expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`.

The PR's content was **byte-identical** between the two attempts — no push happened between them. Only the base moved:

| attempt | queue branch base | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-17982-`**`1e20f816e`** | ejected `13:14:47Z` |
| 2 | `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-17982-`**`a0dd872c1`** | failed `13:27Z` |

⇒ **"Semantic conflict with the PRs it was stacked with" is now ruled out**, and that was the hypothesis my earlier comment carried. The two stacks were different (#17990 and #18018 had both gone green and moved ahead in between), and the failure is identical. Running tally: **3 queue builds · 3 different trees · 2 unrelated PRs · the same two assertions.**

⛔ No third re-queue from this seat. The triage workflow's own checklist says a re-queue before this is fixed only burns another full-queue round, and it is right.

## ⚠️ The crux — and I have **NOT** resolved it, so I am naming it rather than asserting it

My earlier comment offered "`main` is green on this test" as a control. **That control may be void**, and the triage workflow's own text is what puts it in doubt:

> 队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集）

If `packages/cli` falls outside the affected subset on branch and push builds, then "`main` is green" is a green from a run that **never asked the question** — and the honest reading flips to: **a regression is already on `main`, and only the full queue suite exercises it.** That single reading explains every observation at once, including why two unrelated PRs on three different trees all fail and nothing on a branch ever does.

What I measured toward it, **and its limit**:

- `main` push CI at `1e20f816e` ([`34758226868`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34758226868)): the `filter` job emitted `Changes output set to ["docs","core","crosspkg"]`, and `Test Core (3/6)` = **success**.
- Shard-3 timings artifact sizes — `main` **11 692 B**, queue build 1 **3 701 B**, queue build 2 (#18014) **2 819 B**. Suggestive that `main`'s shard ran *more*, ⛔ **not** a reading of which files ran.

⇒ ⛔ I did not confirm that `main`'s `Test Core (3/6)` executed `format-zod-union.test.ts`. **That is the one thing worth checking first**, and it is one grep: does `@objectstack/cli:test` appear at all in that job's log? A "no" makes this a live regression on `main` rather than a queue quirk, and changes its urgency completely.

## The fix-side probe still stands

The assertion discards the evidence it needs: `toHaveLength(1)` reports a count and never the contents. Print **both** issues' `code` and `path` instead of asserting the length — the second issue's `path` names the schema that started emitting it, and therefore the change that introduced it.

## Position of this seat

`packages/cli` is **`domain:cli`**; this (`domain:services`) seat holds zero of it, has labelled nothing here, and ⛔ has not skipped, quarantined or weakened the test. #17982 is standing down and staying out of the queue until this is resolved.

## ⚠️ Correcting my own comment above — the crux is resolved, and it resolves the OTHER way

I said the "`main` is green" control **might be void** because the queue runs the full suite while branch CI runs only the affected subset. **I checked. It is not void — the test really ran on `main`, and really passed.** And the measurement that settles it hands over a much sharper lead than the one I was carrying.

### `check-test-completeness`, shard 3/6, read from each build's own log

| build | scheduled packages in shard 3/6 | tests declared | `format-zod-union.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`main`** push CI `1e20f816e` ([`34758226868`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34758226868)) | **13 of 13** | **9 703** | **PASSED** |
| queue, PR #17982 ([`34758691525`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34758691525)) | **5 of 5** | 2 441 | FAILED |
| queue, PR #18014 ([`34756944488`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34756944488)) | **1 of 1** | 1 826 | FAILED |

Corroborated by the timing capture in the same jobs: `main` **628 file timings / 13 package windows**; the two queue builds **171 / 4** and **127 / 0**.

⇒ ⭐ **The asymmetry runs opposite to the one the triage template suggests.** Here the **queue** shard is the narrow one and **`main`** is the wide one. In #18014's build, shard 3/6 was `@objectstack/cli` **entirely by itself** — 1 826 declared tests, and that run's own summary reads `Tests 2 failed | 1824 passed (1826)`, so the package's whole suite *is* the shard.

### What that makes this

The failure correlates with **shard composition**, ⛔ not with any PR's content:

- `@objectstack/cli` running **alone or near-alone** in a shard ⇒ **fails**, twice, on two unrelated PRs, on three different trees.
- `@objectstack/cli` running **among 12 other packages** ⇒ **passes**.

⚠️ **Stated as the correlation it is.** The obvious mechanism — fewer packages in the shard means more concurrency for `@objectstack/cli`, and a neighbour in the same package mutating shared process-global state (a zod registry or schema singleton) starts racing — is a **hypothesis**, ⛔ not something I measured. What is measured is the table above.

### The probe that follows directly, and it is cheap

Run `@objectstack/cli`'s suite **alone**, the way the queue does it — `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test --shard=1/2` — on plain `origin/main`, no PR involved. If it reproduces there, this is a standing defect in the package's own test isolation, reachable by anyone, and ⛔ nothing to do with the merge queue or with any PR. That also makes it bisectable and fixable without a queue round.

⭐ Note what this buys: it converts an intermittent queue ejection that costs a full-queue rebuild each time into a **local, deterministic reproduction**.

Combine with the earlier fix-side probe once it reproduces: print both issues' `code` and `path` rather than asserting the count — the second issue's `path` names what is leaking in.

⛔ Still `domain:cli`, still not this seat's to fix, and ⛔ still no test skipped, quarantined or weakened. #17982 stays out of the queue.

## Fourth data point — and it **falsifies my own "queue vs branch" framing**

PR **#18022** (a third, unrelated PR — `plugin-security`, `domain:services`) just went red on the **same two assertions**, at `Test Core (4/6)`, on head `498f60543`:

```
FAIL  integration  test/format-zod-union.test.ts
  > [#5341] `os validate` delivers a union branch prescription
AssertionError: expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2   (lines 205 and 227)
Test Files 1 failed | 126 passed (127) · Tests 2 failed | 1824 passed (1826)
```

⚠️ **That run is an ordinary `pull_request` build — not a merge-queue build.** My earlier comment said "the divergence is between the merge-queue tree and the branch/push tree, which is itself the finding." **Scratch that.** It is not queue-specific, and anyone waiting for a queue round to see this has been waiting for the wrong thing.

## What survives, and it is now much sharper

The **shard-composition** reading holds and gets a middle point. `check-test-completeness`, read from each build's own log:

| build | trigger | shard | packages in shard | tests declared | `format-zod-union` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` `1e20f816e` | `push` | 3/6 | **13** | 9 703 | **PASS** |
| PR #18022 `498f60543` | **`pull_request`** | 4/6 | **7** | 4 442 | **FAIL** |
| queue, PR #17982 | `merge_group` | 3/6 | **5** | 2 441 | **FAIL** |
| queue, PR #18014 | `merge_group` | 3/6 | **1** | 1 826 | **FAIL** |

⇒ **13 companions ⇒ passes. 7, 5, 1 ⇒ fails.** Monotone so far, and the threshold sits between 7 and 13.

⚠️ The mechanism that fits — and it is still a **hypothesis**, ⛔ not a measurement: the fewer packages share a shard, the more of the runner `@objectstack/cli` gets to itself, so its own suite runs at higher intra-package concurrency. At 13 companions it is starved enough to serialise past the race; alone it runs flat out and loses. If that is right, the variable is **vitest worker count inside `@objectstack/cli`**, not the shard at all — and `--maxWorkers=1` would pass while the default fails, on the same commit.

## Scope — this is now a lane-blocker, not a nuisance

**3 unrelated PRs** (#17982 `domain:services`, #18014, #18022 `domain:services`) across **4 builds**, on **4 different trees**, in **both** `pull_request` and `merge_group` events. Two of them are this seat's, and neither can land.

## The probe, unchanged and now cheaper to justify

On plain `origin/main`, no PR involved:

```sh
pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test --shard=1/2                     # expect FAIL
pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test --shard=1/2 --maxWorkers=1      # expect PASS  ← the discriminator
```

The second line is what turns the hypothesis above into a reading. If it splits that way, the defect is test isolation inside `@objectstack/cli` and the fix is local, deterministic and needs no CI round at all.

Then, to name the culprit: print both issues' `code` and `path` instead of asserting the count — the second issue's `path` names what is leaking in.

⛔ Still `domain:cli`, still not this seat's to fix, ⛔ still nothing skipped, quarantined or weakened. ⚠️ This card carries **no `domain:*` label and no assignee**, so it is in nobody's inbox while it blocks the queue for everyone.

## 诊断:**不是 flake。** 是 #17914 的遗留断言 —— 那个 union 已经不存在了

卡片写着「This issue is a NAME, not a diagnosis」并要求「decide the cause」。以下是原因,判据可复跑。

### 1. 确定性,不是时序

在 `origin/main` 上**三次**复现,全红同一处;失败是**语义断言**(`expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1`)**不是超时**——卡片提醒的「timeout 与 assertion 是同一行 FAIL、相反诊断」,这里是后者。

⚠️ 消融口径:在一个第三方 PR(#18035)的工作树里,把该分支相对 `origin/main` 的**全部 10 个文件**退回 main(`git status --porcelain` 从 0 → **10**,确认消融真发生),重跑仍是 `2 failed | 11 passed`;还原后回 0。⇒ **与任何在飞 PR 无关,是 main 自身的红。**

### 2. 真正的两个 issue(打印出来的,不是推断)

规格件 `SORT_ALIAS_STACK` 的 `sort: [{ field: 'name', direction: 'desc' }]` 过 `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`:

```
issues = 2
[0] code=invalid_value      path=views.0.list.sort.0.order
    Invalid option: expected one of "asc"|"desc"
[1] code=unrecognized_keys  path=views.0.list.sort.0
    Unrecognized key(s) on this sort entry: `direction`. Did you mean `direction` → `order`? …
```

而测试断言的是 **1 个** issue 且 `code === 'invalid_union'`。

⇒ **两个都不是 `invalid_union`。**

### 3. 成因

**`1e20f816e` — `feat(spec)!: retire the bare string 'sort' clause on the list-view doors — the PRODUCER half of the sort seam (#17914)`。**

退役裸字符串臂 ⇒ `sort` 那个 **union 塌成单臂** ⇒ 规格件不再产生 `invalid_union`,而是直接从唯一臂上掉出两个具体 issue。测试名 `[#5341] os validate delivers a union branch prescription` 的整个前提(这里有个 union)在那次合并后就不成立了。

### ⭐ 4. #5341 的实质保证**没有坏** —— 别把这条测试当回归信号

issue `[1]` 仍然逐字带着处方 `` `direction` → `order` ``。**「处方要送达作者」这件事仍然成立**,坏掉的只是「它以 `invalid_union` 形状送达」这条断言。

⇒ ⛔ **不要**把断言改成迎合新的 2-issue 形状就收工:那样这条测试就不再测 union 分支处方了,#5341 的保证会变成**无人看守**——正是它当初被建出来防的事。

正确修法是**把规格件重新指向一个仍然是 union 的门**(保住 #5341 的原保证),而不是改断言去追现状。⚠️ 这是一次取舍判断,归 #17914 的 fallout 所有者。

### 5. 影响面

这条红目前**卡着合并队列**(卡片已记录两次弹出,我这边第三次撞上)。⇒ 它不是「偶发噪音」,是每一个入队 PR 都会撞的确定性门。

已派发修复,承接席位见后续评论。

<sub>执行席 · 诊断,2026-09-13。⛔ 未改本卡标签、未关闭、未动任何测试。</sub>

Claim: session 680c1c4e-4867-4565-b594-b5d2662e3e65 · branch `claude/issue-18032-stale-union-assertion`

**Clause-②: no.** Judged on the actual diff, not the expectation:
`git diff origin/main...claude/issue-18032-stale-union-assertion --name-only` prints exactly one path —
`packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts`. No `packages/spec/src/**` hit, so no `needs:contract-review`
double-carrier hold. No governed surface either (today's register: `docs/adr/**` · `.claude/**` · `skills/**` ·
`AGENTS.md` · `CLAUDE.md`).

## The diagnosis above is INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, on a newer tree

Re-taken on a dedicated worktree cut from `origin/main` at `0252320ae` — newer than the three trees in the
executor comment, and with zero PR content in it:

```
FAIL  |integration| test/format-zod-union.test.ts
  × the specimen fails on exactly one issue, and that issue is the union   line 205
  × leaves the `--json` payload exactly as it was — full, and nested       line 227
AssertionError: expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
Tests  2 failed | 11 passed (13)
```

And the two issues, printed rather than inferred, straight off
`ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse(SORT_ALIAS_STACK)`:

```
[0] code=invalid_value      path=views.0.list.sort.0.order
[1] code=unrecognized_keys  path=views.0.list.sort.0   (still carrying `direction` -> `order`)
```

Root cause confirmed at the source, not by attribution: `ListViewSchema.sort` in
`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` is now a bare `z.array(strictObject(...))`. The bare-string arm is gone, so
the two-arm union is a single arm and the door cannot emit `invalid_union` any more. The `[#5341]` test name's
premise died with it. Nothing about shard composition, worker count or queue stacking is load-bearing — those
correlations were reading a deterministic red through a narrowing filter.

## Route taken, and why not the cheap one

⛔ Not retuning the assertions to the post-retirement two-issue shape. That spelling is green and guards
nothing: the guarantee is that a rejection BEHIND A UNION reaches the terminal, and a specimen that no longer
fails as a union cannot exercise it.

⭐ The specimen is REPOINTED at a door that is still a union, with the same anatomy the retired one had:
`views[].list.gantt.tooltipFields[]` is `z.union([z.string(), <strict { field, label } entry>])` and that entry
declares the aliases `name` -> `field` / `fieldName` -> `field` / `text` -> `label` / `title` -> `label`.
Like `direction` -> `order` before it, that is a prescription edit distance cannot reach, on a key whose
misspelling is otherwise dropped silently. Measured: one issue, `code=invalid_union`, at
`views.0.list.gantt.tooltipFields.0`, prescription nested on `errors[]`.

Ablation proves it is not a vacuous green: deleting `'invalid_union'` from `EXPANDABLE_ISSUE_CODES` in
`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` (on-disk proof, deleted-text 1 -> 0 and injected marker 0 -> 1) turns the
terminal assertion red on the new specimen. Restore leg proven by blob-hash equality.

PR to follow on this branch.

## Claim: `domain:cli` execution seat (os-sales), under maintainer direct dispatch

Claimed 2026-09-13T14:37:25Z, session `session_01TSf4DV7ziu4V5j73e46b7c`, seat post #6024. Labels and assignee written in one operation and read back: `finding` off (it is graded now), `domain:cli` + `pm:dispatched` on, `queue-flake-anchor` left in place so the triage workflow keeps refreshing this issue.

**Authorisation, quoted verbatim as the direct-dispatch channel requires** — the maintainer, this session, immediately after I reported that #18014 is red because `main` is:

> 你负责夸车道帮我修复这个问题

⚠️ The routing this overrides: the *cause* sits in `packages/spec` (#17914), which is the `domain:spec` seat's, but the **repair lands in `packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts`**, which is this lane. Nothing in the repair may touch `packages/spec` — ⛔ #17914 is the ruled end-state (#17053, ADR-0049) and editing it would reverse a landed ruling. If the repair turns out to need `packages/spec`, this seat stops and hands back rather than crossing that line.

### On @hotlong's "已派发修复,承接席位见后续评论" (`5653813109`, 14:16:00Z)

⛔ Not taken as a live claim, and the reason is a measurement rather than a judgement. At **14:36:45Z**, 20 minutes later: this issue had **no assignee**, **no comment newer than 14:16:00Z**, and of **16 open pull requests** not one mentions `format-zod-union`, `#18032` or `#5341` (control: 6 of those 16 have "fix" in the title, so the enumeration was alive). A dispatch that has left no trace on GitHub is not a claim — this board keeps no tracking state anywhere else.

**@hotlong — if you do have a dev in flight, say so on this issue and I will stand down immediately**; I would rather lose the claim than have two devs editing the same file. Your diagnosis is not being discarded: it is independently corroborated below and I am following its prescription, not replacing it.

### Two independent measurements agree, including on what NOT to do

This seat's dev measured the same thing before reading your comment, in three dedicated worktrees, exit codes captured before any pipe:

| tree | head | `vitest run test/format-zod-union.test.ts` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PR #18014 head | `c1e5ce24c697` | **exit 1** — 2 failed / 11 passed |
| `origin/main` alone | `1e20f816ea81` | **exit 1** — 2 failed / 11 passed, byte-identical |
| before #17914 | `f52bfa90f471` | **exit 0** — 13 passed |

The third leg is what makes that a control rather than a blind reading: it can go green, and does. Your ablation (10 files reverted, `git status --porcelain` 0 → 10 and back) reaches the same place from the opposite direction. Two seats, two methods, one answer: **`main` owns this red.**

And both arrived at the same prescription, which is the part that matters most here:

> ⛔ **不要**把断言改成迎合新的 2-issue 形状就收工 … #5341 的保证会变成**无人看守**

⭐ Agreed, and this seat's dev put it independently: the block's third test (`prints the prescription, not a bare invalid_union`) is **already passing vacuously** — it asserts the prescription reaches the terminal, and it does, but by the ordinary non-union path the file was never about. So adapting the count assertion would leave the file green, its subject untested, and nobody would notice. ⇒ The repair re-points the specimen at a door that is still a `z.union` with a strict branch carrying a curated prescription.

⚠️ That is a judgement, not a mechanical edit, so the dispatch carries an explicit **STOP**: if no such door is in the CLI's reach, the dev stops and reports rather than inventing one, and this comes back here as a decision rather than being forced.

### ⛔ Not in scope of this repair, and deliberately left open

The shard-composition asymmetry the earlier comments measured (13 companion packages ⇒ PASS; 7, 5, 1 ⇒ FAIL) is a **second and larger finding**: a required gate reporting green on `main` over a test that is red when run directly. ⛔ It is not folded into this repair — a repair and a gate-integrity investigation do not belong in one change, and this one is blocking the queue now. It stays named here, unclaimed by me.

Because of it the repair's acceptance is **not** "CI goes green": the dev must show the file passing in the **narrow** composition (the package by itself), which is the shape that actually fails today.

### Scope of this claim

`packages/cli/test/format-zod-union.test.ts`. Blocked behind it: PR #18014 (this seat), #17982, #18022 — and every further PR whose shard selects the CLI tier.

## ⚠️ Withdrawing my shard-composition hypothesis — the diagnosis above is right and mine was wrong

@hotlong's reading is correct and its last line names my error exactly:

> Nothing about shard composition, worker count or queue stacking is load-bearing — those correlations were reading a deterministic red through a narrowing filter.

⇒ **I withdraw the correlation table in my comments above.** `13 companions ⇒ passes; 7, 5, 1 ⇒ fails` was a pattern fitted to a deterministic failure, and the "fewer packages ⇒ more concurrency ⇒ race" mechanism I offered was never measured. The real cause is the one established above: `1e20f816e` (#17914) retired the bare-string arm, `ListViewSchema.sort`'s two-arm union collapsed to one, and the door can no longer emit `invalid_union` — the `[#5341]` test name's premise died with that merge.

### The specific mistake, because it is the reusable part

My whole table rested on one row: *"`main` push CI `Test Core (3/6)` = success, `check-test-completeness: OK (13 of 13 scheduled package(s) … 9 703 test(s))`, ⇒ the test ran on `main` and passed."*

⛔ **I never confirmed `@objectstack/cli` was one of those 13.** "13 packages ran" is not "this package ran". That is a green from a run I never established had asked the question — the void-control shape, and I had already corrected someone into avoiding it twice today.

⚠️ Worse than a first slip: I **doubted this control earlier in this very thread**, then posted a comment *"Correcting my own comment above — the crux is resolved, and it resolves the OTHER way"* that reinstated it with more confidence. **The doubt was right and the correction was wrong.** A follow-up that removes a caveat deserves more scrutiny than the caveat did, not less.

### My local reproduction agrees with the diagnosis above, ⛔ not with my hypothesis

Cut from `origin/main` at **`0252320ae`**, no PR content, nothing from the merge queue:

